institutionName: UiT The Arctic University of Norway

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That the university could provide the courses i wanted.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: quite easy. Everything is on the websites, so its was very manageable.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Samskipnaden - a study-organisation I think, was super helpfull, all ready from the airport, with handing out keys and giving directions to get on the right busses. Super nice after travels, I felt very welcome.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Well it was student housing, just not on campus... But still easy, you just needed patience, cause they tell you quite late if you have gotten one or not. So just apply for housing as soon as you put in the first application.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's a very nice community around the student housings.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was online, so you had to do it through "Studentweb". But nothing big to worry about.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: It was very helpfull to email the student coordinater of UiT, he was always quick to respond.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the courses I wanted, but something was wrong with one of them, so I only heard about that course on the day it started. At that time I already decided to skip that, and go with the other ones, since I had enough points to so...

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you end up having questions, just email the coordinater.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Well, being a BA-student, it was a bit terrifying to take MA-courses, though they were very interesting, so it made up for the higher level courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very similar.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
All kinds, I feel like.
Knitting group
waffle friday
all kinds of sports, both teams and individual

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Join the knitting group. Its free, you learn how to knit, there free cake, tea and coffee, and they help you get started. Its very chill. 

Join TSI, they will definately find an activity for you if you like.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go to Senja, it's so beautiful.
Sign up for "Turbo", a place you can borrow outdoor equipment for free, so lack of gear doesn't keep you away from joining hikes, cabin trips and so on... Make full use of your stay.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, people are very friendly.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Local students are hard, because they already have their groups, but if you have classes with them, ask them for help and they are more than willing to do that.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Tromsø is clearly a very international town, many tourist all year around, and especially people from university og the hospital are the major part of the culture, though if you really want norwegian culture, you should take a little drive out of the main city.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The diversity, everybody is welcome everywhere.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Apply for student housing as soon as possible.
2. Join the intro days - you might find the people you will hang out with for the rest of your stay.
3. The professors are very sweet! Don't hesitate to ask a question, they will be more than happy to help you understand.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Use Mazemap to find your way around Campus.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: crossing the line of asking professors questions. It's something I will take back home with me. I learned to be a more independent student without my student-group from home. Very rewarding and I come back with confidence that I can do this study!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Asking professors without feeling stupid.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: It has been a really nice stay!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
